target.title: Suppress model fallback notices in rooms
target.body:
## Summary

Suppress model fallback transition and fallback-cleared status notices when the source chat is a group or channel room.

Fallback state is still persisted and lifecycle events are still emitted, so diagnostics remain available without posting internal model-routing details into shared conversations.

## What Problem This Solves

Model fallback notices are operational diagnostics that can include selected and fallback model names plus provider/auth error text. They currently bypass normal source-reply suppression, which is useful in direct chats but can expose internal model-routing state in shared rooms such as WhatsApp monitoring groups.

This PR keeps direct-chat diagnostics unchanged while preventing fallback transition and fallback-cleared notices from being delivered to group or channel conversations.

## Changes

- Skip building fallback notice payloads for `ChatType: "group"` and `ChatType: "channel"`.
- Keep direct-chat notices unchanged.
- Keep fallback state persistence and lifecycle events unchanged.
- Add e2e coverage for suppressing fallback transition and fallback-cleared notices in room contexts.
- Update model-failover docs to describe the room suppression behavior.

## Evidence

- Local guard verification on the installed runtime: `scripts/ensure-openclaw-fallback-notice-guard.sh --check` confirmed the room fallback-notice guard is present and made no changes.
- Local syntax validation of the installed runtime patch: `node --check /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw/dist/agent-runner.runtime-BriI2__w.js` passed before restarting the Gateway.
- Live observation after restart: `openclaw status --all` reported the Gateway running and Telegram/WhatsApp accounts OK.
- PR branch validation: `git diff --check` passed.
- Full test suite was not run for this targeted external PR.
